title: Instrumentation policy linter and deployment safeguard for latency SLOs
creator: Asha Menon
description: Add a CI-time instrumentation policy linter and a runtime deployment safeguard that prevent services from shipping changes which would degrade latency SLOs. This ticket covers: (1) a linter that enforces required trace hooks and metric emission patterns, (2) a gating check that runs synthetic SLO probes and anomaly detectors against pre-release clusters, and (3) a small set of standardized burn-rate alert templates and paging policy recommendations to be attached to services by default.
acceptance_criteria: CI linter exists as a GitHub Action that fails PRs when required tracing hooks or metric labels are missing
Pre-deploy job runs synthetic probes (p95 latency + error rates) against the canary environment and blocks rollout if projected burn-rate > 1.5x for 15m window
New burn-rate alert templates (low/medium/high) are published in the alerting catalog and selectable via service config
Console displays a per-service instrumentation score and flags missing trace/span attributes used for SLO attribution
Runbook generated for common failure modes and automatic mitigations (automatic rollback, non-pager run for transient noisy regressions)
Integration tests exercising linter, probe job, and template selection included in pipeline
implementation_notes: Linter: implement as TypeScript GitHub Action using AST checks for language-specific SDKs and regex checks for config files (supports Go, Python, Node SDKs).
Trace hooks: require root span -> service.name and span attribute 'redwood.request_id'; produce a machine-readable JSON report consumed by console ingestion hook.
Metrics/log checks: ensure presence of latency histogram (labels: route, model_variant) and error counters with error_kind label. Linter will accept shim mapping file for legacy services.

Pre-deploy probes: reuse synthetic-probe runner (job from ENG-711111) with 100 concurrent simulated requests over 5m, capture p50/p95/p99 and error ratio. Feed into burn-rate estimator to compute projected SLO burn-rate.
Alert templates: implement three templates parameterized by SLO target, burn-rate threshold, evaluation window, and paging escalation chain. Store templates in alerting-catalog repo.
Console integration: add instrumentation_score endpoint to observability API; score computed from linter report + probe results + metric coverage. Expose in /service/:id/observability.
Anomaly detection: enable lightweight z-score anomaly check as a fallback for services without full model-based detectors; flagged anomalies appear as advisory in pre-deploy job.
Backward compatibility: provide opt-out annotation 'redwood.observability: legacy-allow' documented and gated behind security review for sensitive infra teams.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Linter can cause developer friction by failing many legacy services — Mitigation: ship linter in warning mode for 3 cycles, provide automated fix suggestions and shim mapping file.
Risk: Synthetic probes add noise to canaries and consume quota — Mitigation: limit probe concurrency by service tier and reuse existing canary infra; cost budget tracked in observability project.
Risk: False positive burn-rate estimates may block valid deployments — Mitigation: conservative thresholds with manual override, and add 'allowlist' annotation for rapid unblocking with audit log.

Risk: Attack surface for pre-deploy checks if they access private clusters — Mitigation: run probes from isolated runner inside customer VPCs or dedicated preprod cluster; follow least privilege guidelines.
Risk: Teams opt out of defaults leading to inconsistent coverage — Mitigation: add onboarding checklist and monthly telemetry audit with PM outreach
